subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking runbook, MAP timeline & triage of discrepancies
message_1_subject: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking plan & close timelines
message_1_body:
Hi Jordan / Lina,

Thanks again for the discussion yesterday. Per our MAP, attached is a concise benchmarking runbook we plan to execute this week so we can align on TTFT/latency and concurrency expectations before the pilot close. High-level: 

- Goal: reproduce Acme's production-like workload for the key fulfillment flow (avg seq len ~220 tokens).
- Metrics: median and p95 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, TTFT (time-to-first-token), and concurrency scaling at 1/4/1/2/4x anticipated peak.
- Tooling: we will run both our in-house harness (redwood-perf harness) and a parity run with your JMeter scripts to highlight tooling variance.

Attached: redwood-benchmark-plan-v2.pdf (run steps + config), tooling-compare-sheet.csv (mapping of metrics + measurement hooks).

Ask: can you confirm the target SLA you want validated (latency p95 target and concurrency level)? Also share a small redacted request sample (or allow us to replay the anonymized stream) so our reproduction matches payload distributions.

Goal timeline (MAP):
- 08/11: Redwood runs parity harness on a dedicated cluster and sends initial numbers.
- 08/12–08/13: Customer run and side-by-side comparison; triage discrepancies.
- 08/14: Canary run with tuned config and decision on go/no-go for pilot close on 08/18.

I'll sync Neha and Grace on resources.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan-v2.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), tooling-compare-sheet.csv (CSV, 1 sheet)
message_2_subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking plan & close timelines
message_2_body:
Sergio —

Thanks for the plan and the clear timeline. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) SLA: target p95 token latency <= 220ms for the fulfillment streaming endpoint, TTFT <= 120ms for single-request interactive flows.
2) Concurrency: our expected steady peak is ~60 concurrent users, spike to 240 for flash events. Can you validate at 60/120/240?

We will prepare a sanitized sample stream and Lina will share a JMeter test plan by EOD. Please also call out how you will measure TTFT (client-visible vs server-side first-token). We've seen tooling differences in the past where JMeter captures different timing hooks.

—Jordan
Jordan Price | Head of Platform, Acme Logistics
jordan.price@acme-logistics.com
+1 (617) 555-2244
message_3_subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking plan & close timelines — run details
message_3_body:
Hi all,

Quick note on methodology so expectations are aligned before any runs: 

- TTFT measurement: we will report both server-side first-token (time from request received on the server until first token emitted by the runtime) and client-observed TTFT (including network latency). Reported TTFT in runbook is server-side by default; we will annotate client-side deltas when we replay your sanitized stream from your region.
- Harness parity: we will run (A) redwood-perf harness (uses persistent HTTP/2 streaming, warm KV cache, continuous batching) and (B) JMeter parity using your artifacts. We will publish raw traces and per-request timing breakdowns.
- Environment: Dedicated cluster (g5dn-equivalent), quantization profile: int8-fast for cost parity. Kernel selection notes included in the PDF.

I attached the updated plan (same redwood-benchmark-plan-v2.pdf) and tooling-compare-sheet.csv with the exact timing hooks we will extract.

Next steps: we (Redwood) will run the A harness 08/11 morning and share consolidated numbers by EOD. Please send the sanitized stream ASAP.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan-v2.pdf, tooling-compare-sheet.csv
message_4_subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance benchmarking plan & close timelines — Acme run results
message_4_body:
Team —

We completed our parity run against the production-like cluster. Summary (attached acme-ttft-sample-logs.zip):

- Observed median token latency roughly in line with Redwood's numbers, but p95 is ~1.8x higher than your published redwood-perf harness at the same concurrency.
- TTFT (client-observed) is often ~250–350ms depending on region; your server-side TTFT numbers look lower per your report.
- At 240 concurrency we see a sharp throughput drop consistent with kernel thrashing on our GPU instance (we're running an older driver).

We captured raw per-request traces and our JMeter timing hooks. I included a short excerpt below: 

> On Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 10:21 AM neha.kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> > Quick note on methodology so expectations are aligned...

We suspect two potential causes for the p95 delta: (1) tooling differences (JMeter vs redwood-perf) causing different TTFT capture points, and (2) driver/kernel/quantization differences on our side. We'll provision a small test host with updated drivers to rule out infra.

Sharing logs now. Lina
Lina Zhou | Infra Lead, Acme Logistics
lina.zhou@acme-logistics.com

Attachments: acme-ttft-sample-logs.zip (ZIP, 8MB)
message_5_subject: Re: MAP: discrepancy triage plan & next actions
message_5_body:
Jordan / Lina —

Thanks for the thorough run and logs. Proposed triage steps to isolate the p95 delta: 

1) Reproduce: Redwood will replay your sanitized stream from the same region and run both harnesses (redwood-perf and JMeter) against a matched driver/kernel configuration. Expected by 08/13 EOD.
2) Driver parity: please try an updated GPU driver on one host (Lina noted she'll provision) and share results; this will tell us if kernel thrash is the root cause.
3) Timing parity: we'll publish a short shim that converts our server-side first-token hook into a JMeter-compatible client-side hook so we compare apples-to-apples.
4) Competitive comparison: we will also run a short reference against VendorX's endpoint (non-prod, identical config) to characterize whether the delta is model vs infra. We'll surface a single summary matrix.

If reproductions show tooling is the primary cause, we will update the MAP acceptance criterion to include a tooling-aligned p95 measurement. If infra is the cause, we will provide a recommended driver/kernel/quantization bundle and a patch-level config.

Proposed next MAP milestone: 08/14 morning — joint canary with updated driver + shimmed timing. If that passes p95 <= 220ms and TTFT server-side <= 120ms, we keep the 08/18 pilot close. Otherwise, escalate for a short architecture workshop.

CC'ing Grace to schedule the canary window.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
